Goooood morning. Today we have to talk about gun violence. In a weekend slated to be full of art fairs and food festivals, at least nine people were shot in two different shootings, and three people were killed. We all know this, but let’s say it out loud: This isn’t normal. The Second Amendment does not trump the right to survive in public. It should not be this easy to end a life.
Let’s do the news.
Mass Shooting at Seattle Center: During the last hours of the Bite of Seattle, at least one gunman opened fire in the crowd near the Armory. They killed three people, and injured four more. Police haven’t released any of their names, but one of the injured is a 2-year-old boy.
As of this morning, three of the injured victims have been released from Harborview. The toddler is still at the hospital. One suspected shooter is in custody, and SPD is still looking for a second person they believe was involved. “There may be more,” Assistant Police Chief Tyrone said. “We’re still trying to figure this out.” Based on the weapons found at the scene, SPD believes the gunmen were trying to shoot at each other. If you witnessed the shooting, they want to talk to you at 206-233-5000.
Information moved too slowly last night. Seattle police didn’t hold a news conference until almost 11 p.m.—leaving the public with just one vague update to “please avoid the area” for almost five hours. A Seattle Police Department spokesperson told KOMO that the conference was delayed because some dignitaries wanted to attend the news conference. Representative Pramila Jayapal attended the late-night conference, as well as Mayor Katie Wilson.
Seattle Center is still closed to the public while vendors come back to close up their stands. The Pacific Science Center is closed today as well. If you have tickets for anything at the museum today, they’ll be automatically refunded.
More Gun Violence: Late on Friday night, two people were shot on Capitol Hill at Pike and 11th—one at A-Pizza Mart and another at Wildrose. Based on security footage, police think the victims were innocent bystanders of a shootout between people on the street. They’re both in stable condition.
In Less Horrifying Crime News: Two men bought tickets for the Space Needle on Friday night, rode the elevator up, went out onto the observation deck, climbed over the glass wall, and parachuted off of it. They landed safely on the ground, and didn’t appear to hurt anyone else. Police would like to charge them with first-degree criminal trespassing, but they haven’t been able to find them.
It’s Officially Jimothy Summer: Is a meme still a meme if our local government endorses it? Yesterday, near the Ballard Farmer’s Market, Councilmember Alexis Mercedes Rinck declared Summer 2026 “Jimothy Summer.” The event included a call-and-response of “round” and “boi,” and a Jimothy art competition. The winner was a Saint Jimothy stained glass piece, but I’m partial to the delightfully round Jimothy piñata.
Weather: It’s warming up a little today. Expect highs in the upper 70s, partly cloudy, you know the drill.
Fucked Around, Finding Out: Economists are sounding the immigration alarm again. On Monday morning, in the name of “protecting American jobs,” the Trump administration will revoke about 350,000 immigrants’ work permits, with another 190,000 expected to get pulled in September. All of these workers, largely from Haiti and El Salvador, were protected under the humanitarian Temporary Protected Status program until last month when the Supreme Court gave Trump the OK to end it. But it turns out losing half a million workers isn’t good news for the American economy. The US Chamber of Commerce is lobbying Congress to push back. Even Republican elected officials in Florida and Ohio are calling it a “mistake.”
If you remember one quote from the NYT story about Temporary Protected Status, let it be this from Stephen Miller:
Stephen Miller, an architect of Mr. Trump’s immigration agenda, was asked after the T.P.S. ruling if Haiti is safe.
“For Haitians? Absolutely,” Mr. Miller said. “Haitians live in Haiti. It’s not our position that Haitians should leave Haiti. It’d be crazy for us to say that Haitians couldn’t live in Haiti. It’s their country.”
Haiti has been engulfed in violence since the assassination of its last elected president in 2021. Large swaths of the capital Port-au-Prince are controlled by gangs that have attacked, kidnapped and killed civilians, causing the internal displacement of more than one million people. The country’s economy is in ruins, and international aid organizations report widespread food insecurity.
Trump Tries to Hide the Cost of War: The Pentagon has changed how they report deaths in the Iran War, splitting them into categories on two separate webpages in an apparent effort to hide the total number of lives lost. As of today, 18 Americans have been killed in the war with Iran. One website logs the deaths in Operation Epic Fury, tallied at 14. Another logs “Overseas operations casualties starting July 7, 2026,” which includes the other four. Sean Parnell, the chief Pentagon spokesman, said any claims that the Pentagon was trying to conceal the total number of deaths were “fabrications.” Sure.

Three killed, four wounded in Seattle food festival shooting, police say
- By Reuters -
- Jul 27, 2026
SEATTLE: Three people were killed and four others, including a toddler, were wounded in a shooting at a downtown Seattle food festival, police said, adding that a suspect had been taken into custody.
A second suspect was also believed to be involved, and officers were searching for that person, Seattle Police Department Assistant Chief Tyrone Davis said in a media briefing late on Sunday.
Davis said the police believed two people were shooting at each other. The incident took place at the Bite of Seattle food festival at Seattle Center.
“What happened here today at the Seattle Center was an unbelievable tragedy, and a horrific act of violence,” Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson said during the joint media briefing with the other officials.
“We have far too much gun violence in this city and in this country, and we’re coming off of a week in Seattle where we’ve had three major incidents of gun violence in just a few days,” she added.
Officials did not disclose the motive of the shooting.
NO ONGOING THREAT TO THE COMMUNITY
Seattle police’s Davis said the suspect in custody was a “young person,” but declined to disclose more details, and also said they did not have a description for the suspect at large.
Local media had earlier reported that there were two deaths and five injuries.
Davis said one person in hospital died of their injuries, bringing the toll to three. He added that the four others in hospital were now in stable condition.
“There were two people who we believe were shooting at each other,” Davis said. Asked whether the gang unit had been called in, he said several detectives, including homicide and gun violence reduction units, were on scene.
“Right now, we believe that we have no outstanding threat to the community,” Davis said.
“We do have one suspect that is being interviewed.”
Davis said the police recovered two guns at the scene,but stressed that the investigation was still ongoing.
Witnesses had told the Seattle Times that they heard several shots around 6 p.m. local time (0100 GMT).
Police said officers “responded and addressed one of the shooters” after they heard gunshots in the area.

sources.news_title: Police search for second suspect following Seattle festival shooting that killed 3
sources.text:
SEATTLE — Police now say there were at least three suspects involved in a food festival shooting near Seattle’s Space Needle over the weekend, and that one of them was among those killed in the violence.
In a document filed in juvenile court in Seattle, where a 15-year-old arrested in the case was making an initial appearance Monday, police said they believe there were at least three shooters: the 15-year-old; an acquaintance who died at the scene; and “at least one other unknown suspect.”
“Based on the evidence at the scene, investigators believe” the 15-year-old “and one of the deceased engaged in a gunfight with at least one other unknown suspect,” the document said.
The teen was being held in juvenile detention for investigation of firearms violations and first-degree assault ahead of the afternoon court appearance, Mayor Katie Wilson said at a news conference.
Authorities said earlier Monday they are still looking for an additional suspect, but could not rule out whether that individual was among those killed.
“We are trying to identify who that person is,” said Seattle Police Chief Shon Barnes.
Investigators had said they believed the two suspects were shooting at each other. Police said late Sunday night it was not clear whether any of the victims had been involved in the confrontation between the two shooters.
Two people died at the scene and a third died at a hospital. They were described as two men, ages 19 and 44, and a woman, 56.
The four wounded included a 2-year-old boy, who was in satisfactory condition Monday. The others — two men, ages 23 and 27, and a woman, 39 — were discharged, a hospital spokesperson said.
Vendors were allowed to return to the sprawling campus Monday morning to clean up and collect their equipment and merchandise. Skewered squid on grills, roasted ducks in ovens and plates full of food were among the items left behind as people fled the gunfire.
Near the spot of the shooting, a stain of what appeared to be blood was still visible in the morning. A candlelight vigil was planned Monday night at the center’s International Fountain.
The gunfire erupted around 6 p.m. Sunday in the waning hours of the Bite of Seattle. The annual three-day festival draws hundreds of food and retail vendors and performers to Seattle Center, a sprawling park and event space in the shadow of the Space Needle. Many attendees rushed into campus buildings or ran from the park at the sound of the shots.
Dozens of officers were providing security at the event and some saw one of the suspects firing, authorities said. A large number of police and emergency crews responded and began evacuating the area. Police then searched an IMAX theater on the grounds where they initially believed a second shooter had fled.
Adam Lombardo, who had a Burmese food stand at the festival with his spouse, described the panic of fleeing people as a “stampede.” As he gathered his equipment Monday, he described how police escorted them into the crime scene to turn off their ovens and stoves.
“It’s really sad because you think that three innocent people aren’t getting up with their families,” he said. “They just came to enjoy a food festival with people, with friends, with new friends, and they lost their lives in just what sounds like meaningless bloodshed.”
Festival attendee Faith Adia Hunter said she and her friends had just gotten food from a crepe vendor when gunfire broke out nearby. In the scramble to find safety, she and others ran into the nearby Seattle Children’s Museum.
“We were about to start eating, then heard someone yell something, then we saw people start to run,” Hunter said. “So we took off running, too.”
Roberto Ramirez, a vendor at the event, said he heard what sounded like firecrackers before people began yelling “shooter” and frantically running.
“Suddenly everything was empty,” he said. “People were freaked out.”
After the initial panic, new guests continued to arrive, unaware of what had happened. Police told them to leave, he said.
Estan Wakonabo said he and his girlfriend were waiting in line for a photo booth when he was shoved from behind and turned to see a rush of people fleeing.
“People were hiding, were pushing, people were falling on the ground, baby strollers were falling,” Wakonabo said, adding that was when he heard gunshots.
“Once I heard a ‘pop, pop, pop,’ that’s when I knew it was a shooter,” he said.
After he escorted his girlfriend to safety, he returned to the scene to take photos and saw multiple victims on the ground, Wakonabo said.
The festival started in 1982 and draws 350,000 attendees, according to its website.
Associated Press journalists Manuel Valdes and Lindsey Wasson in Seattle, Annika Wolters in Bangkok and Christopher Weber in Los Angeles contributed to this report.

Livestream Captures Gunfire, Panic at Bite of Seattle Festival as 3 Are Killed, Multiple Wounded, Including Toddler
A festive evening turns tragic as gunfire erupts at Seattle's popular food festival, leaving multiple casualties.
A food vendor's livestream at the Bite of Seattle festival captured the moment gunfire shattered a crowded Sunday evening, leaving three people dead and at least four others injured, including a toddler.
The clip was streamed by Hawaiian Honey Cones, one of the vendors at the annual food festival held at Seattle Center. In the video, the vendor appears to be speaking to viewers when a colleague suddenly shouts, 'Shooting!' Panic can then be seen and heard as people begin fleeing the area.
The livestream, which was being used to promote the festival, recorded the immediate aftermath of the shooting near the food stalls. Festivalgoers had gathered for food, music and family activities at Seattle Center before the gunfire broke out.
Three Dead, Four Wounded
Seattle police said the shooting happened at about 6 p.m. on Sunday during the Bite of Seattle festival, a three-day event that attracts hundreds of food vendors, retailers and live performers.
Three people were killed. According to the Seattle Police Department, the victims were a 19-year-old man, a 44-year-old man and a 56-year-old woman. Two died at the scene, while the third died later at Harborview Medical Center.
Four other people were taken to hospital, including a 2-year-old boy. Officials said early Monday that the surviving victims were in stable condition. Authorities have not released additional details about the victims' identities pending notification of their families.
Police Say Two People Exchanged Gunfire
Investigators believe two people were shooting at each other outside the Seattle Center Armory when bystanders were struck.
One suspect was arrested at the scene, while police continued searching for another person believed to have been involved.
Assistant Seattle Police Chief Tyrone Davis said there was no ongoing threat to the public, but investigators were still working to determine what led to the shooting.
Police recovered two firearms from the scene, according to Reuters. Officials also said there were no surveillance cameras in the immediate area, making witness accounts, mobile phone footage and public tips important to the investigation.
Multiple agencies responded, including the Seattle Police Department, Seattle Fire Department and federal law enforcement. The FBI said it was aware of the shooting, while agents from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives also attended the scene.
Investigation Continues After Festival Shooting
Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson described the shooting as an 'unbelievable tragedy' and 'a horrific act of violence.'
She said the city was focused on supporting those affected and assisting investigators as they worked to establish what happened.
Witnesses told local media they saw people running for cover after the gunfire erupted, with some seeking shelter inside nearby buildings around Seattle Center.
The Bite of Seattle festival continued earlier in the weekend before Sunday's shooting brought the event to an abrupt halt in the affected area. Police have not said whether the incident was connected to the festival itself or whether the suspects were known to one another.
Investigators are continuing to review evidence, interview witnesses and examine video footage recorded by members of the public, including the livestream shared by Hawaiian Honey Cones. Authorities have asked anyone who witnessed the shooting or captured footage of the incident to contact detectives.
Seattle police have asked anyone with information to contact investigators as homicide and gun violence detectives continue their investigation.

In a document filed in juvenile court in Seattle, where a 15-year-old arrested in the case was making an initial appearance Monday, police said they believe there were at least three shooters: the 15-year-old; an acquaintance who died at the scene; and “at least one other unknown suspect.”
“Based on the evidence at the scene, investigators believe” the 15-year-old “and one of the deceased engaged in a gunfight with at least one other unknown suspect,” the document said.
The teen was being held in juvenile detention for investigation of firearms violations and first-degree assault ahead of the afternoon court appearance, Mayor Katie Wilson said at a news conference.
Authorities said earlier Monday they are still looking for an additional suspect, but could not rule out whether that individual was among those killed.
“We are trying to identify who that person is,” said Seattle Police Chief Shon Barnes.
Investigators had said they believed the two suspects were shooting at each other. Police said late Sunday night it was not clear whether any of the victims had been involved in the confrontation between the two shooters.
Two people died at the scene and a third died at a hospital. They were described as two men, ages 19 and 44, and a woman, 56.
The four wounded included a 2-year-old boy, who was in satisfactory condition Monday. The others — two men, ages 23 and 27, and a woman, 39 — were discharged, a hospital spokesperson said.
Vendors were allowed to return to the sprawling campus Monday morning to clean up and collect their equipment and merchandise. Skewered squid on grills, roasted ducks in ovens and plates full of food were among the items left behind as people fled the gunfire.
Near the spot of the shooting, a stain of what appeared to be blood was still visible in the morning. A candlelight vigil was planned Monday night at the center’s International Fountain.
The gunfire erupted around 6 p.m. Sunday in the waning hours of the Bite of Seattle. The annual three-day festival draws hundreds of food and retail vendors and performers to Seattle Center, a sprawling park and event space in the shadow of the Space Needle. Many attendees rushed into campus buildings or ran from the park at the sound of the shots.
Dozens of officers were providing security at the event and some saw one of the suspects firing, authorities said. A large number of police and emergency crews responded and began evacuating the area. Police then searched an IMAX theater on the grounds where they initially believed a second shooter had fled.
Adam Lombardo, who had a Burmese food stand at the festival with his spouse, described the panic of fleeing people as a “stampede.” As he gathered his equipment Monday, he described how police escorted them into the crime scene to turn off their ovens and stoves.
“It’s really sad because you think that three innocent people aren’t getting up with their families,” he said. “They just came to enjoy a food festival with people, with friends, with new friends, and they lost their lives in just what sounds like meaningless bloodshed.”
Festival attendee Faith Adia Hunter said she and her friends had just gotten food from a crepe vendor when gunfire broke out nearby. In the scramble to find safety, she and others ran into the nearby Seattle Children’s Museum.
“We were about to start eating, then heard someone yell something, then we saw people start to run,” Hunter said. “So we took off running, too.”
Roberto Ramirez, a vendor at the event, said he heard what sounded like firecrackers before people began yelling “shooter” and frantically running.
“Suddenly everything was empty,” he said. “People were freaked out.”
After the initial panic, new guests continued to arrive, unaware of what had happened. Police told them to leave, he said.
Estan Wakonabo said he and his girlfriend were waiting in line for a photo booth when he was shoved from behind and turned to see a rush of people fleeing.
“People were hiding, were pushing, people were falling on the ground, baby strollers were falling,” Wakonabo said, adding that was when he heard gunshots.
“Once I heard a ‘pop, pop, pop,’ that’s when I knew it was a shooter,” he said.
After he escorted his girlfriend to safety, he returned to the scene to take photos and saw multiple victims on the ground, Wakonabo said.
The festival started in 1982 and draws 350,000 attendees, according to its website.

Associated Press journalists Manuel Valdes and Lindsey Wasson in Seattle, Annika Wolters in Bangkok and Christopher Weber in Los Angeles contributed to this report.

“It was just pure chaos,” he said.
He said he came back to the scene later to take photos, and saw several gunshot victims on the ground, including a body covered with a yellow sheet.
A Seattle Police Department spokesperson, reached by phone, said he was on his way to the incident and had no further information.
The fire department said it treated five other people at the scene: a woman, 40, with minor injuries; and a 39-year-old woman, a 2-year-old boy, a 23-year-old man, and a 56-year-old woman, all of whom were taken to the hospital.
Harborview Medical Center said that all four patients who arrived had suffered gunshot wounds. A hospital spokesperson said the 56-year-old woman was in surgery and in critical condition, while all others were in satisfactory condition.
Kayla Carris, 22, was sitting outside the Seattle Center Armory at the Bite of Seattle when people began to scream and run to get inside the armory.
“Everyone was just throwing stuff and running,” Carris said. “Like everyone.”
Paul Skinner, 47, had just returned from grabbing drinks for his staff at his Filipino food booth, when he heard a series of pops.
“I just heard what sounded like what were some pretty loud fireworks at first,” he said. “Then, the energy changed. Mobs of people started flooding back down. I just told our staff to get down.”
A video posted to social media appeared to show the moment gunshots first rang out.
“Shooting! Shooting!” a man says.
“Get down, get down, get down,” another yells, as crowds start to run.
Todd Behrends, 59, said he heard what sounded like several rounds of shots.
People began running and jumping over each other to get away. One woman fell, and someone stepped on her leg, he said. As he also ran toward an exit, he saw a woman on the ground and a man in a stretcher.
It was unclear if police had anybody in custody as of 7 p.m.

A spokesperson for Harborview Medical Center, the highest-level trauma care center in the region, said they would be receiving patients from the incident.

A suspect is in custody and a second remains at large after a shooting at a food festival in Seattle on Sunday evening left three people dead and four others wounded, according to police. Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson said police arrested a 15‑year‑old in connection with the attack, which unfolded near the Space Needle during the Bite of Seattle festival.
Caleb Mitchell, 30, told Newsweek early on Monday that he posted a video on TikTok, where he uses the handle "leebotracks," raising concerns about the lack of security measures after visiting Bite of Seattle with his girlfriend on Friday.
In the video, he claimed attendees were able to enter the annual food festival held beneath Seattle’s Space Needle with "no security, no pat down, no search to the bag."
Newsweek has contacted Bite of Seattle for comment via an email sent outside regular business hours.
Mitchell, an artist who also owns a marketing agency, said the festival had numerous entry points with no security checks.
"The first thing we noticed was we could just walk straight in through the parking lot," he said.
His concern was heightened because he was able to bring a handgun, which he said he has a license to carry, into the festival.
"It was shocking," he said. "Because if I wasn't checked, that means how many other people here have firearms?"
Mitchell said he had purchased the weapon because of safety concerns.
"If there's no security checkpoint and it comes down to where I have to defend myself and the people that I'm with, I have an opportunity to," he said. "If there's a checkpoint and I see it, I'm going back to my car, I am safely securing it in the lock box, and going back without my firearm."
Mitchell said there were security guards at the festival, but he viewed the number as insufficient. As someone with experience hosting events, Mitchell said the city requires event hosts to have at least three to four guards for every 100 attendees.
"For the amount of people that were there, it seemed like there was only two or three people every, like 200 to 300 yards. You would hardly see any security walking around," he said.
Mitchell added that he would not attend the Bite of Seattle festival in the future even if security measures were ramped up.
"There should have been a statement out within hours, apologizing or just letting people know to stay safe, stay covered. There have not been any statements," he said.
"So due to that, I just feel like there's not really a lot of love for the people. And my intentions when I made that video was out of a sense of safety and support for the people."
Mitchell also addressed the shooting in a video posted late on Sunday night.
"I tried to let everybody know how security was being handled," he said in the video. "Nobody can say I didn't try to let people know. People really were bashing me in my comment sections on the previous videos."
He told Newsweek: "The type of backlash that I got was I was not man enough, I was scared, and that I am just trying to make a viral video." He added: "As a Black man, I just think that it's important to put safety first."
It is unclear what security measures were in place at the festival. Last year, organizers said they had a "strong record of security" after a vendor complained about a break-in.
Bite of Seattle began in 1982 and draws more than 350,000 attendees over "three days of food, drink, and community celebration" at the Seattle Center, according to its website.

Three people died and four others were injured, including a toddler, after gunfire erupted at the festival at around 6 p.m. on Sunday.
Two of the victims died at the scene and a third died at a hospital. The four injured, including a 2-year-old boy, were hospitalized and in stable condition, said Grace Nuñez, a spokesperson for the Seattle Fire Department. The rest of the injured were adults.
Police arrested one suspect and were looking for another, Assistant Seattle Police Chief Tyrone Davis told a news conference Sunday night. However, he said that there was no ongoing threat to the public. Investigators believe the two suspects were shooting at each other, Davis said, adding that two guns were recovered from the scene.
Rep. Pramila Jayapal, whose district includes Seattle Center, said she was “absolutely horrified” by the shooting and noted that officials were “coordinating across all levels of government.” “My heart goes out to the victims, their families, and our whole Seattle community,” she wrote on X.

Three people have been killed and others injured after a gunman opened fire at a food festival in Seattle.

Reportan tres muertos y varios heridos en tiroteo en festival gastronómico de Seattle, según autoridades
Por Julianna Bragg, CNN
Tres personas murieron y al menos otras cuatro, incluido un niño, resultaron heridas en un tiroteo la noche del domingo durante un festival gastronómico en Seattle, a una cuadra del icónico Space Needle de la ciudad, informaron las autoridades..
El tiroteo del domingo por la noche en el Bite of Seattle, un evento gratuito que cada año atrae a cientos de miles de asistentes, desató el pánico entre el público. Un numeroso grupo de personas fue visto derribando una cerca para escapar tras una ráfaga de disparos, en el más reciente episodio de la violencia armada que afecta a estadounidenses mientras realizan actividades cotidianas.
Las autoridades respondieron a reportes de un tiroteo poco después de las 6 p. m. en el Seattle Center.
“Hubo unos seis o siete disparos, múltiples disparos”, dijo Justice Beitzel, quien estaba comiendo con amigos mientras un concierto se desarrollaba cerca, a Ben Hunte, de CNN. “De repente vi a la gente corriendo hacia nosotros”.
Dos personas fueron declaradas muertas en el lugar. Otras cuatro, entre ellas un niño de 2 años, fueron trasladadas al Harborview Medical Center, informó el departamento de bomberos. Posteriormente, otra persona llegó por sus propios medios a otro hospital con una herida de bala, según las autoridades.
Una de las víctimas murió posteriormente en un hospital, informó la noche del domingo el subjefe de la Policía de Seattle, Tyrone Davis.
Un sospechoso, descrito únicamente como una “persona joven”, fue detenido. Las autoridades continúan buscando a una segunda persona que se cree estuvo involucrada, dijo Davis.
Más temprano, la alcaldesa de Seattle, Katie Wilson, había dicho que había dos personas bajo custodia, pero luego corrigió esa información.
Según Davis, se cree que dos personas se estaban disparando entre sí. Las autoridades recuperaron dos armas. La investigación sigue en curso y “no existe una amenaza activa para la comunidad”, afirmó.
Aún se desconoce qué motivó el tiroteo. Las autoridades pidieron a quienes presenciaron el ataque que aporten cualquier información que pueda ser útil para la investigación.
El tiroteo es uno de al menos 271 tiroteos masivos registrados en EE.UU. este año, según el Gun Violence Archive, que define un tiroteo masivo como aquel en el que cuatro o más personas reciben disparos.
El Seattle Center se describe como un espacio cívico, artístico y familiar que recibe a más de 12 millones de visitantes al año para eventos realizados en su campus de 74 acres, donde se encuentran el Space Needle y la principal arena de la ciudad. El festival Bite of Seattle reúne a cientos de vendedores locales y presentaciones de música en vivo, y atrae a unas 350.000 personas durante tres días, según su sitio web.
Videos compartidos en redes sociales mostraban a multitudes caminando entre los puestos de vendedores al aire libre antes de que los disparos provocaran una estampida.
Uno de los vendedores estaba transmitiendo en vivo cuando comenzó el tiroteo. El video, emitido por el puesto de comida Hawaiian Honey Cones, muestra a un hombre hablando a la cámara mientras se escuchan al menos cuatro disparos de fondo.
Luego se observa a las personas agacharse y correr para alejarse del lugar. Un numeroso grupo de asistentes también fue captado derribando una cerca para escapar del área.
Dos testigos dijeron a KOMO, afiliada de CNN, que escucharon “entre siete y ocho disparos” y que la gente corría “por todas partes”. Un hombre contó que estaba cerca de un escenario donde tocaba una banda cuando escuchó “al menos dos docenas de disparos”, informó KOMO.
Otro hombre dijo que algunas personas no reaccionaron de inmediato porque pensaron que “debían ser fuegos artificiales o algo así”. Pero, después de escuchar más disparos, vio a la gente “irrumpiendo por toda el área” para intentar salir.
Algunas personas parecieron refugiarse en la tienda de regalos del Space Needle, según un video compartido con CNN.
Videos mostraban a policías, personal de emergencia y agentes de varias agencias, incluido el FBI, en el lugar tras el ataque.
En un audio de los servicios de emergencia obtenido por CNN, se escucha a una persona solicitar un “torniquete pediátrico” para una víctima en la escena.
Un equipo SWAT del estado de Washington también se dirigía al lugar para colaborar, a solicitud de la Policía de Seattle, informó el gobernador Bob Ferguson.
CNN se comunicó con la Policía de Seattle, autoridades municipales, el Seattle Center, el FBI y la Oficina de Alcohol, Tabaco, Armas de Fuego y Explosivos (ATF).
La alcaldesa calificó el tiroteo como “un acto de violencia atroz” y dijo que la comunidad “intenta entender cómo un evento dedicado a la cultura, la conexión y la alegría terminó en un intercambio de disparos”.
“En los próximos días estableceremos qué ocurrió y seremos transparentes con el público sobre lo que hayamos aprendido”, escribió Wilson. “Esta noche, nuestra atención está puesta en las personas que perdieron la vida, quienes luchan por recuperarse y las familias que permanecen a su lado”.

Any witnesses who might have information on potential suspects are encouraged to call (206) 233-5000.
The suspect in custody, a young individual, is currently being interviewed by SPD. The department will release more details Monday morning.

The Bite of Seattle event was taking place at the Seattle Center during the shooting. Bite of Seattle, the largest free-admission food event in Washington, was scheduled to occur from 11 a.m. to 8 p.m. Friday through Sunday.

More than 350,000 people were expected to attend the three-day event.

For years, the Bite has been one of Seattle’s signature summer traditions. To see violence at a place that brings so many people together is heartbreaking and unacceptable. My heart is with the victims and their loved ones, those who were senselessly injured, Seattle Center employees and vendors, and everyone who has been traumatized by the experience. I am also grateful for the first responders who rushed in to protect others and care for the injured.”
Shortly after, Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson published a statement.
“What happened at the Seattle Center today was an act of horrific violence,” Wilson wrote. “Impacted families are living through the worst moment of their lives, and an entire community is trying to understand how a gathering built around culture, connection, and joy ended in gunfire. No one should have to weigh the risk of being shot before attending an event, gathering with friends, or experiencing their city.”

sources.text:
SEATTLE – Police arrested one suspect and were looking for another after gunfire erupted at a crowded food festival beneath Seattle's Space Needle, leaving three people dead and four others injured, including a toddler.
Investigators believe the two suspects were shooting at each other and, although one remained on the loose, Assistant Seattle Police Chief Tyrone Davis told a news conference Sunday night that there was no ongoing threat to the public.
Recommended Videos
Police did not have a description of the outstanding suspect, he said.
“We’re still trying to figure this out,” Davis said.
Two people died at the scene and a third died at a hospital. The four wounded, including a 2-year-old boy, were hospitalized and in stable condition, said Grace Nuñez, spokesperson for the Seattle Fire Department. The rest of the injured were adults. Davis couldn't say if any of the victims were involved in the confrontation.
The gunfire erupted around 6 p.m. in the waning hours of the Bite of Seattle, an annual three-day festival that draws hundreds of food and retail vendors and performers.
Dozens of officers were providing security at the event and some saw one of the suspects firing, Davis said. One suspect surrendered at the scene, but the other fled. Law enforcement searched the grounds to no avail.
A large number of police and emergency crews responded and began evacuating the area around the sprawling Seattle Center campus.
Faith Adia Hunter said she and her friends had just gotten food from a crepe vendor when gunfire broke out. She realized a shooter was near them. She and others found shelter in the nearby Seattle Children’s Museum.
“We were right next to him when it started so we took off running,” Hunter said. “So we took off running too into the building with the crowd.”
In the chaos, many vendors bolted toward the exits, abandoning their food stands. Hours afterward, some milled outside the police tape, wondering when they would be allowed to return to collect their tents, food and cooking gear.
Roberto Ramirez, a vendor at the event, said he heard what sounded like firecrackers before people began yelling “shooter” and frantically running.
“Suddenly everything was empty,” he said. “People were freaked out.”
After the initial panic, new guests continued to arrive unaware of what had happened and were told by police to leave, he said.
Estan Wakonabo said he and his girlfriend were at the festival waiting in line for a photo booth when he was shoved from behind and he turned to see a rush of people fleeing.
“People were hiding, were pushing, people were falling on the ground, baby strollers were falling,” Wakonabo said, adding that was when he heard gunshots.
“Once I heard a ‘pop, pop, pop,’ that’s when I knew it was a shooter,” he said.
After he escorted his girlfriend to safety, he returned to the scene to make photos and saw multiple victims on the ground, Wakonabo said.
The annual festival started in 1982 and draws 350,000 attendees over “three days of food, drink, and community celebration,” according to its website.
___
Associated Press journalists Manuel Valdes and Lindsey Wasson in Seattle, Annika Wolters in Bangkok and Christopher Weber in Los Angeles contributed to this report.

sources.news_title: Three people killed, several injured in shooting at Bite of Seattle food festival
sources.text:
A 15-year-old has been detained in connection with Sunday’s shootout at the Seattle Center that involved at least two others — one of whom was killed, The Associated Press reported.
The shootout killed a 56-year-old woman and two men, ages 19 and 44, police said.
Police said in a document filed in juvenile court they believe there were at least three shooters: the 15-year-old, an acquaintance who died at the scene, and “at least one other unknown suspect, according to the AP.
“Based on the evidence at the scene, investigators believe” the 15-year-old “and one of the deceased engaged in a gunfight with at least one other unknown suspect,” the document said, according to the AP.
Authorities earlier said they believed two people were shooting at each other, according to Seattle Assistant Police Chief Tyrone Davis, who said there is no ongoing threat to the public.
There were at least seven victims caught in the crossfire, possibly eight, authorities said in a Monday news conference.
Police are asking for those with information about the shooting to come forward.
The shooting at the Bite of Seattle, a free event that draws hundreds of thousands of guests each year, sent attendees running for their lives. A large group was seen knocking down a fence to escape after a volley of gunfire, the latest gruesome entry in the ever-expanding log of Americans victimized by gun violence while doing everyday activities.
Authorities responded to reports of shots fired just after 6 p.m. at the Seattle Center.
“There were about six or seven, multiple gunshots,” Justice Beitzel, who was eating with friends as a concert played nearby, told CNN’s Ben Hunte. “All of a sudden, I just saw people running towards us.”
Two people were declared dead at the scene. Another person died after being taken to a local hospital, Davis said late Sunday.
In emergency dispatch audio obtained by CNN, one person was heard requesting a “small child tourniquet” for a victim at the scene.
A 2-year-old boy was taken to Harborview Medical Center, the fire department said Sunday. By Monday morning, the toddler remained at the hospital in “satisfactory condition,” according to Susan Gregg, the hospital’s media relations director.
A few other victims were seen at local hospitals, including a 23-year-old man and 39-year-old woman who have since been discharged from Harborview, and a 27-year-old man who was released from nearby UW Medical Center – Montlake, Gregg added.
Police recovered two weapons at the scene. It’s not clear what prompted the shooting.
Police said the 15-year-old suspect, who surrendered on scene, was booked into the Judge Patricia H. Clark Children and Family Justice Center on investigation of firearms violations and first-degree assault.
The teen is expected in court Monday afternoon, where a judge will determine whether there was probable cause for the arrest, the King County Prosecuting Attorney’s Office said in a statement.
Police have not formally arrested anyone for investigation of homicide in relation to the shooting, Barnes said.
The shooting is one of at least 271 mass shootings in the US this year, according to the Gun Violence Archive, which defines a mass shooting as one in which four or more victims are shot.
The Seattle Center spans a 74-acre campus and is home to the Space Needle and the city’s largest arena, drawing more than 12 million visitors each year. And hundreds of thousands of those visitors bring their appetites to the center for the annual Bite of Seattle Festival, which hosts hundreds of local vendors offering creative foods and live entertainment across three days.
Crowds of people walked through the aisles of outdoor vendors Sunday, passing plates of poke, bowls of noodles and freshly grilled seafood. Social media users gleefully documented their cheese pulls and noodle swirls in videos shared online.
As shots were fired, the jovial mood turned to panic. Festival-goers rushed to flee the danger.
A livestream from food vendor Hawaiian Honey Cones captured a man speaking to the camera as at least four gunshots rang out in the background.
People ducked and ran from the scene as a large group of attendees knocked down a fence on their way out of the area.
In the aftermath of the chaos, witnesses shared varying accounts of what they saw and heard.
Two witnesses told CNN affiliate KOMO they heard seven to eight gunshots, as people ran in all directions. Another attendee said he was near a stage where a band was performing, when he heard at least two dozen shots.
Another man said some people didn’t react right away, thinking, “Oh it must be fireworks or something.” But after more shots were heard, he saw people “storming through the area” trying to get out.
Some people appeared to take shelter in the gift shop of the Space Needle at the Seattle Center, video shared with CNN showed.
Police, emergency responders and officers from several agencies, including the FBI, were at the scene afterward, video showed.
A Washington state SWAT team was also on its way to assist at the request of Seattle police, Gov. Bob Ferguson said.
CNN has reached out to Seattle police and city officials, as well as the Seattle Center, the FBI, and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives.
Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson called the shooting “an act of horrific violence” and said the community “is trying to understand how a gathering built around culture, connection, and joy ended in gunfire.”
“In the days ahead, we will establish what happened and be transparent with the public about what we have learned,” Wilson wrote. “Tonight, our attention belongs to the people whose lives were taken, those fighting to recover, and the families beside them.”
This story has been updated with additional information.
Correction: An earlier version of this story incorrectly attributed a quote that was said by Seattle Police Chief Shon Barnes and incorrectly reported the age of one victim.
CNN’s Sara Smart, Hanna Park, Amanda Watts, Jamie Gumbrecht and Josh Campbell contributed to this report.

- A 15-year-old suspect in the shooting and one person who died at the scene Sunday night are believed to have been in a gunfight with “at least one other unknown suspect,” according to court documents. Anyone with information is encouraged to call 206-233-5000; tips can be provided anonymously.
- A candlelight vigil in honor of the shooting victims is scheduled to take place at 8:30 p.m. on Monday at the Seattle Center's International Fountain.
Pacific Science Center remains closed in wake of shooting
The Pacific Science Center will remain closed Monday, July 27, following Sunday's shooting at the Bite of Seattle. All screenings at its IMAX theater have been canceled for the day.
The center will reopen under normal hours on Tuesday, July 28.
According to a statement from the Pacific Science Center, an IMAX screening of "The Odyssey" was halted and the audience was evacuated around 6:30 p.m. Sunday. At the same time, the center went into lockdown as police responded to the scene of the shooting nearby and searched for suspects.
Staff were allowed to return to the building at around 10:35 p.m.
“The safety of our visitors and staff is always PacSci’s top priority," Pacific Science Center CEO and President Kevin Malgesini said in a statement. "Our staff receives regular training on safety procedures, including active shooter training."
His statement continues, "Our thoughts are with the victims, those injured and their loved ones, and our focus going forward is on continuing to take care of our team, our guests and our Seattle Center community.”
‘Associate’ of detained shooting suspect among the dead; police searching for third person of interest
A 15-year-old suspect in the Seattle Center shooting and one person who died at the scene Sunday night are believed to have been in a gunfight with “at least one other unknown suspect,” according to court documents.
“At the time [the 15-year-old suspect] was taken into custody, an associate of his who was detained at the same time died of a gun shot (sic) wound,” according to court documents reviewed by KUOW. “A witness observed [the suspect in custody] firing south into a crowd of people where four victims were standing near the vendors and struck by gun fire.”
The report noted thousands of Bite of Seattle attendees and hundreds of vendors were present when the 15-year-old suspect fired into the crowd.
Authorities are still looking for at least one more person involved and have asked anyone with information to call the SPD tipline at 206-233-5000.
Prosecutors seek probable cause for first-degree assault against shooting suspect
Prosecutors are seeking probable cause for three counts of first-degree assault and one count of second-degree unlawful possession of a firearm against a 15-year-old suspect arrested in connection with Sunday’s deadly shooting.
The suspect did not appear in King County Superior Court Monday afternoon. His parents were present for Monday’s hearing via Zoom.
KUOW is not naming the suspect because he is a juvenile and has not been formally charged.
An arraignment was set for Thursday at 9 a.m.
In the meantime, Judge Tanya Thorp said the suspect will remain in secure detention and have no contact with victims or their families.
Mayor, police chief defend themselves against criticism over shooting communication lag
Seattle and Washington state officials on Monday defended themselves amid criticism over delays in addressing the public with information about Sunday’s shooting at the Seattle Center.
A press conference was promised at 9:45 p.m. Sunday, more than four hours after reports of the shooting had first emerged. But that press conference was delayed for another hour.
Seattle Police spokesperson Brian Pritchard told KUOW and other members of the press at about 10:33 p.m. Sunday that the delay was because officials were “waiting for dignitaries.” When officials did address the public at 10:48 p.m., Gov. Bob Ferguson and U.S. Rep. Pramila Jayapal were in attendance alongside Mayor Katie Wilson and Acting Police Chief Tyrone Barnes.
During a press conference Monday, Wilson denied the press conference delay was because they were waiting for Ferguson, Jayapal, or any other officials.
“That is absolutely not the case,” Wilson said in response to a direct question about the matter. “Last night at Seattle Center, what we had was a scene of an active investigation where SPD was searching the grounds for a possible second suspect. There are times when elected officials' presence is not helpful, and that was one of those times. We don't want our law enforcement distracted taking care of elected officials when they have work to do.”
Ferguson’s office also denied he was the reason for the delay.
A spokesperson for the governor said he was in Olympia when he received word of the shooting at about 7 p.m., then he immediately drove to Seattle. He was within 10 minutes of Seattle Center by 9 p.m., and at 10:10 p.m., he was told there would be media availability at the center. According to the spokesperson, he immediately left for the center and arrived around 10:30.
Jayapal’s office shared a similar timeline, noting the congresswoman was briefed at home over Zoom at 8 and 9 p.m. before she was also notified about a press conference at 10:10. She went to the center from her home in Seattle.
A statement from Wilson’s office was also quietly corrected. Her office initially said two suspects were in custody, but that was corrected to say that just one person had been taken in.
Asked about the discrepancy Monday, Wilson said, “In complex situations like this, information flies around. And so, that initial report that we got of two suspects in custody was incorrect, and that's part of why it's taken us a while to be able to stand here and say, ‘This is accurate information.’”
Seattle Police Chief Shon Barnes on Monday also defended himself when a reporter asked about his whereabouts during the shooting. Barnes was out of town Sunday at the time of the shooting but returned to Seattle after he got word of the shooting.
“ I wish that I had a crystal ball and, and we could schedule gun violence, but we can't,” Barnes said during the press conference. “Yesterday, I was in Dallas at the National Organization of Black Law Enforcement Executives conference. It's their 50th anniversary. At that conference, two members from our community were being honored.”
When pressed by South Seattle Emerald reporter Connor Nash later, Barnes was visibly frustrated.
“I have been here working as hard as I can for this city from the day I got here. Do you got that?” Barnes told Nash.
Nash continued to ask about “reports that [Barnes is] not in town often.”
“The reports are wrong. Do you understand?” Barnes said as another man tried to usher him away from reporters and others who were filming. “Do you understand?”
Shooting victim count could be 8, city officials say
There may have been an additional victim in Sunday's Seattle Center shooting, potentially bringing the victim count up to eight, Seattle Fire Chief Harold Scoggins said Monday morning.
Officials have not yet named any of the victims.
The three victims who died include a 19-year-old male and 44-year-old male who died at the scene. A 56-year-old female died after being transported to Harborview Medical Center Sunday night.
Confirmed shooting victims who survived include:
- A 44-year-old who declined medical transport.
- A 39-yr-old female transported to and released from Harborview.
- A 23-year-old male transported to and released from Harborview.
- 2-year-old male transported to Harborview, where he remains in satisfactory condition
Officials say they are working to confirm whether a 27-year-old male transported to and released from UW Medical Center-Montlake with a gunshot wound was injured in the Seattle Center shooting. 
Suspect in custody is 15-year-old, set to appear in court Monday afternoon
The suspect taken into custody Sunday night is a 15-year-old who is believed to have opened fire into the crowd at Bite of Seattle.
During a press conference Monday, Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson said the teen would appear in court for the first time at 1:30 p.m.
Wilson said authorities believe two people were exchanging gunfire, but another suspect has not yet been located.
Police Chief Shon Barnes could not say whether the shooting was gang-related but said that it was “group related.”
'Lost things’ Reddit thread documents the debris of a tragedy
A patchwork blanket made of jeans. A pacifier covered in dirt. A bright blue spoon with a bite of food still waiting on it. These are just a few items left behind at Seattle Center Sunday night and documented on Reddit Monday morning.
User “--veggielover--” posted a gallery of various items strewn across the area, including many single shoes left behind in the rush to get away.
“I took a walk this morning around my usual route through Seattle Center. I was taken back by the frozen in time scene of chaos,” the user wrote on the forum. “They were starting to clean up but there was so much to do. ... I didn’t touch anything, just captured it where it was.”
Witness Jessica Allison told KUOW Sunday night how she and her husband took off running with their daughter after they heard the shots. Allison was waiting to see whether she’d be allowed back into the venue to collect her daughter’s blanket when she recounted what she’d seen.
It may be some time before people are reunited with their belongings.
Seattle Center spokesperson Jayme Stocker said the center has not yet coordinated how people can get their things. For now, anyone with questions about lost and found items can call the customer service line at 206-684-7200.
Stocker said the center will be issuing a statement later today.
Reddit user “--veggielover--” also noted food scattered at the scene where “crows were going nuts” in the aftermath. One photo showed what appeared to be a lobster split in half, sitting in a spilled pile of noodles on the pavement. Another captured an eerily empty Vietnamese street food stall with takeout containers and rolls at the ready.
Candlelight vigil planned to honor shooting victims
A candlelight vigil in honor of the shooting victims is scheduled to take place at 8:30 p.m. on Monday at the Seattle Center's International Fountain.
Several shooting victims released from hospital
Two shooting victims taken to Harborview Medical Center on Sunday have been discharged.
As of Monday morning, Harborview Medical Center spokesperson Susan Gregg said the hospital has only one remaining shooting patient: a 2-year-old boy who is in satisfactory condition. The hospital has discharged a 23-year-old male and 39-year-old female.
Additionally, a 27-year-old male has also been discharged from UW Medical Center-Montlake, Gregg said. It's unclear whether his gunshot wound is related to Sunday's shooting at the Seattle Center.
Elected officials respond to shooting
Elected officials from Seattle expressed gratitude toward first responders as the city waited for more information about what led to the deadly shooting at the Seattle Center Sunday night.
“I am absolutely horrified by the shooting that took place this evening at Seattle Center,” said U.S. Representative Pramila Jayapal (D-Seattle). “We will continue to do all we can to ensure all federal resources that are necessary are available.”
Seattle City Attorney Erika Evans urged people to continue to avoid the Seattle Center area as the investigation continued.
"What should have been a celebration of our community, our culture, and a place where families could come together was instead shattered by horrific violence,” Evans said in a statement.
Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson also extended thanks to first responders during a press conference Sunday night, which he attended. Ferguson was asked whether he would take action to increase police forces in Washington cities, and he expressed support for such measures.
1 other suspect could be at large, police say
The Seattle Police Department is looking for at least one more suspect in the Seattle Center shooting.
Seattle Police Acting Chief Tyrone Davis said one suspect is in custody, but at least one other person is believed to have been involved and is still at large.
Davis said officers were looking for another suspect in the area around Seattle Center, but he said he does not believe there is an immediate danger to the general public.
Davis said two guns were recovered and authorities believe at least two people may have been shooting at each other, though a motive is unclear.
Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson acknowledged an early statement from her office incorrectly stated that two people were in custody.
Davis also declined to provide information about the suspect already in custody, saying only that they are a “young person.”
Because the area around the suspects was so crowded, Davis said there were certainly witnesses.
“We need people to be brave,” he said. “We need information. We need help to solve this crime.”
Anyone with information is encouraged to call 206-233-5000; tips can be provided anonymously.
Davis spoke to reporters Sunday night in Chief Shon Barnes’ place; Barnes was not in town at the time of the shooting.
Death toll climbs to 3
A third victim in Sunday night's Seattle Center shooting has been pronounced dead, Acting Seattle Police Chief Tyrone Davis said during a press conference.
That victim, an adult female patient, had been taken to Harborview Medical Center in critical condition and put through emergency surgery.
Three other victims, including a 2-year-old boy, remain at Harborview where they are being treated for their injuries.
Festival worker helped children, families escape
Issaiah Flores from Los Angeles was working at one of the carnival games when he heard the gunshots.
But as people fled, Flores said he realized kids and others were trapped in a play area. He quickly started helping them over a fence to get them out.
“I’m carrying everyone’s kids, just throwing them over. Even grown women — just picking them up and tossing them over,” he recalled.
Once he had cleared the area, he said he found his coworkers and left, too.
Estan Wakonabo saw others trying to help people around them.
He and his girlfriend were waiting in line when he felt someone push him.
“I thought someone was trying to be a punk, and I turn around and just,” he paused. “The best way I can describe it is ‘World War Z.’ Everyone’s coming. That’s what I saw: a stampede.”
Rather than take off, he said he grabbed his girlfriend in a bearhug and stood still, “because there’s nowhere to go in front of us.”
He got his girlfriend to safety before running back to see if people needed help.
“One person was doing CPR,” he said. “People were trying to help each other.”
Seattle Mayor Wilson promises transparency in days ahead
As the Seattle Police Department prepared for a press conference Sunday night, Mayor Katie Wilson released a statement promising “we will establish what happened and be transparent with the public about what we have learned.”
Details were scarce, though.
Wilson said it “was an act of horrific violence” and thanked first-responders, Harborview personnel, Seattle Center event staff, and bystanders “who helped people reach safety and provided aid in terrifying circumstances.”
“We know that many people who were not physically injured will carry what they experienced today for a long time," she said in her statement, encouraging anyone experiencing a mental health crisis to call or text the 988 helpline.
“Tonight, our attention belongs to the people whose lives were taken, those fighting to recover, and the families beside them,” Wilson concluded. “Seattle grieves with you, and we will stand with you in the difficult days ahead.”
Witnesses report ‘stampede’ as crowd recognized gunshots
Witnesses described startling scenes to KUOW reporters in the aftermath of the shooting.
Jessia Allison said she was in line for food with her husband and daughter when she heard two or three shots ring out.
“Like pop, pop, pop. And I looked at him, and I'm like, ‘That’s fireworks, right? Like, that’s someone being silly,’” she said. “And then, we heard a spray of bullets.”
Allison heard shots again as people started screaming and running. She and her family ran to hide behind a stage to wait.
“We just didn’t know what to do,” she said. “It was just an absolute stampede.”
Allison was waiting to see if she could get back into the venue space to retrieve her daughter’s blanket when she spoke with KUOW.
Andrew Aguilera said he didn’t initially register the sounds of gunshots as he was working the “break-the-bottle" carnival game before he saw people running.
His friend urged him to run, too, and they took off with a group of people heading away from the area. Aguilera said his friend who told him to run had brought him along to work at the festival.
“ He had asked my mom and everything for permission,” Aguilera said. “My mom would kill him if anything happened to me.”
As Aguilera ran with the crowd, he said he noticed people still waiting to come into the festival.
“I was just telling everyone, ‘Don't go. Like, there's an active shooter. It’s not safe,’” he said.
Shooting survivors arrive at Harborview
Four survivors of Sunday’s shooting at the Seattle Center are being treated for their injuries at Harborview Medical Center.
Those victims include one adult female patient who is in critical condition and undergoing surgery, a 2-year-old male, a 23-year-old male, and a 39-year-old female, Harborview spokesperson Susan Gregg said in a statement.
Their injuries include gunshots to the arm, leg, lower leg, and abdomen, Gregg added.
At least 1 suspect in custody
At least one suspect has been arrested in connection with the shooting of at least six people at Seattle Center on Sunday, an official confirmed to KUOW.
The identity of the suspect has not yet been released.
An official had previously told KUOW that two suspects were in custody.
Two victims have been pronounced dead while at least four others remain injured with gunshot wounds.
Officials have not yet released information about a possible motive for the shooting.
Witnesses recount gunshots
There were repetitive, loud booms and then people in the crowd started to run, according to witnesses who spoke to KOMO news. One vendor told reporters he helped people climb over a short cement wall in search of safety.
The medical response is centered around Fisher Pavilion, located at 2nd Avenue North and Thomas Street.
Seattle Center is a sprawling campus west of downtown that serves as a cultural epicenter for events, arts, sports and health services. The 74 acre site contains more than 30 partner organizations, including the Space Needle, Pacific Science Center, Climate Pledge Arena, and KEXP.
Someone familiar with the incident told KUOW that one of the wounded is a 2-year-old child.
Gunshots can be heard in a live stream video of one of the food vendors, Hawaiian Honey Cones. In the video’s background, people start to clamor over a temporary fence and flee from the campuses central area.
2 dead, 5 others injured
Two shooting victims have died and four others with gunshot wounds have been hospitalized, someone familiar with the incident confirmed to KUOW.
Police later confirmed that a fifth victim had been treated for injuries at the scene.
Police, fire, and medical personnel have responded to the 200 block of Thomas Street in Lower Queen Anne. Officers are trying to secure the area, which saw large crowds this weekend for the annual Bite of Seattle food festival.
Authorities were first alerted to the shooting around 6:00 p.m. on Sunday.

sources.news_title: 2 dead, 5 injured in shooting at Seattle food festival
sources.text:
Police now say there were at least three suspects involved in a shootout at a crowded food festival near Seattle’s Space Needle over the weekend. One of them was among those killed in the violence.
In a document filed in juvenile court in Seattle, where a 15-year-old arrested in the case did not appear for a scheduled initial appearance Monday, police said they believe there were at least three shooters, rather than two: the 15-year-old; an acquaintance who died at the scene; and “at least one other unknown suspect.”
“Based on the evidence at the scene, investigators believe” the 15-year-old “and one of the deceased engaged in a gunfight with at least one other unknown suspect,” the document said.
The teen was being held in juvenile detention for investigation of firearms violations and first-degree assault ahead of the scheduled court appearance, Mayor Katie Wilson said at a news conference. It was not immediately clear why the teen did not appear in court.
The gunfire erupted around 6 p.m. Sunday in the waning hours of the Bite of Seattle, leaving three people dead and at least four others injured. The annual three-day festival draws hundreds of food and retail vendors and performers to Seattle Center, a sprawling park and event space in the shadow of the Space Needle. Many attendees rushed into campus buildings or ran from the park at the sound of the shots.
Officials provided confused statements about the shooting
News that there were at least three suspects followed a series of confused statements from city officials concerning the shooting.
IN CASE YOU MISSED IT | Teen pleads guilty in deadly Georgia high school shooting
On Sunday, the police department waited five hours to share with the public that one shooter was in custody and that they believed another to be on the loose. Earlier, the mayor had wrongly announced two people were in custody.
At a news conference Monday, just two hours before the 15-year-old was due in court, Police Chief Shon Barnes said investigators weren’t sure if the second shooter was among the dead. Neither he nor the mayor made any reference to additional shooters. Barnes had been out of town Sunday, attending a conference of Black law enforcement executives in Dallas.
The officials have defended their handling of the case, saying they were trying to ensure they provided accurate information about chaotic events.
Two people died at the scene and a third died at a hospital. They were described as two men, ages 19 and 44, and a woman, 56.
The four wounded included a 2-year-old boy, who was in satisfactory condition Monday. The others — two men, ages 23 and 27, and a woman, 39 — were discharged, a hospital spokesperson said.
One of the victims was walking a bicycle when struck, the court document said. The toddler was with his mother.
Vendors were allowed to clean up Monday
Vendors were allowed to return to the sprawling campus Monday morning to collect their equipment and merchandise. Skewered squid on grills, roasted ducks in ovens and plates full of food were among the items left behind as people fled the gunfire.
Near the spot of the shooting, a stain of what appeared to be blood was still visible in the morning. A candlelight vigil was planned Monday night at the center’s International Fountain.
Dozens of officers were providing security at the event and some saw one of the suspects firing, authorities said. A large number of police and emergency crews responded and began evacuating the area. Police then searched an IMAX theater on the grounds where they initially believed a second shooter had fled.
Adam Lombardo, who had a Burmese food stand at the festival with his spouse, described the panic of fleeing people as a “stampede.” As he gathered his equipment Monday, he described how police escorted them into the crime scene to turn off their ovens and stoves.

“It’s really sad because you think that three innocent people aren’t getting up with their families,” he said. “They just came to enjoy a food festival with people, with friends, with new friends, and they lost their lives in just what sounds like meaningless bloodshed.”
Attendees describe chaos at a joyful event
Festival attendee Faith Adia Hunter said she and her friends had just gotten food from a crepe vendor when gunfire broke out nearby. In the scramble to find safety, she and others ran into the nearby Seattle Children’s Museum.
“We were about to start eating, then heard someone yell something, then we saw people start to run,” Hunter said. “So we took off running, too.”
Estan Wakonabo said he and his girlfriend were waiting in line for a photo booth when he was shoved from behind and turned to see a rush of people fleeing.
“People were hiding, were pushing, people were falling on the ground, baby strollers were falling,” Wakonabo said.
The festival started in 1982 and draws 350,000 attendees, according to its website.

sources.news_title: Two dead, five injured in shooting at Seattle Center: Officials
sources.text:
SEATTLE, WA — Two people are dead and five others are injured after shots rang out at the Bite of Seattle food festival at the Seattle Center on Sunday, according to officials.
Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson said a suspect has been taken into custody. Further details on the suspect have not been released. The Seattle Police Department said they are investigating.
The Seattle Fire Department said first responders were dispatched to the scene just after 6 p.m.
They attempted lifesaving efforts for two patients, but they were unsuccessful, according to fire officials. Both patients were declared deceased at the scene, SFD said.

The other patients -- a male child, a 23-year-old male and a 39-year-old female -- are in stable condition, according to the hospital.
A 40-year-old female with minor injuries from the scene declined transport to the hospital, according to fire officials.
The shooting occurred during Bite of Seattle, an annual festival with food vendors and live music held at the Seattle Center.
"What happened at the Seattle Center today was an act of horrific violence," Mayor Wilson said in a statement. "Impacted families are living through the worst moment of their lives, and an entire community is trying to understand how a gathering built around culture, connection, and joy ended in gunfire."
"No one should have to weigh the risk of being shot before attending an event, gathering with friends, or experiencing their city," the mayor said.
Multiple agents from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives Seattle field office responded to the incident, an agency spokesperson told ABC News.
The FBI is aware of the shooting, an agency spokesperson said.
